subject: social-studies
title: Water Supply: From Rain to Tap, Stage by Stage

questions.prompt: A student says: Tap water is clean as soon as it is collected, because rainwater and reservoir water are already safe to drink. What is the best correction?

choices.text: The student is right - rain and reservoir water look clear, so they must already be safe to drink
Collected water is raw water, not tap water: it must be drawn to the treatment works and cleaned stage by stage before it is stored and piped to home taps.
The water becomes safe while it travels through the pipes to the treatment works
Reservoir water is tap water because it has been stored for a long time

questions.misconception: Tap water is clean as soon as it is collected, because rainwater and reservoir water are already safe to drink.
questions.explanation: The trap claim is: Tap water is clean as soon as it is collected, because rainwater and reservoir water are already safe to drink. In fact Collected water is raw water, not tap water: it is drawn from the reservoir to the treatment works, where treatment stages remove dirt and germs step by step, and only the cleaned water is stored and piped to home taps.

questions.prompt: What happens to the water at the treatment works in stage 3?

choices.text: It is stored until it becomes clean on its own
It passes through treatment stages one at a time - dirt settles and sinks, and germs are trapped and removed
It is mixed with rainwater to make it cleaner
It is piped straight to home taps

questions.explanation: Scene 3 works this: the water passes through the treatment stages one at a time, dirt settles and sinks, germs are trapped and removed, and the cleanliness bar climbs at every stage.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, state what happens to the water between the reservoir and the treatment works.
questions.answer: The raw water is drawn out of the reservoir and carried through pipes to the treatment works, and moving it does not clean it.
questions.explanation: Scene 2 runs this stage: the water travels from the reservoir to the treatment works unchanged - the cleanliness bar barely moves.

questions.prompt: Explain why the cleanliness bar climbs during treatment in stage 3 but barely moves in stages 1 and 2.
questions.answer: The bar climbs only when dirt and germs are removed: collecting and moving the water remove nothing, but each treatment stage removes more dirt and germs, so the bar climbs 70 to 140 to 210 to 280.
questions.explanation: The bar rises in s3 at every treatment stage - settling, filtering and the final clean - while s1 collecting and s2 moving the water leave it almost unchanged.

questions.prompt: Which list gives the stages of the water supply in order?

choices.text: Rain collected in a reservoir, raw water drawn to the treatment works, treatment cleans the water stage by stage, clean water stored and piped to home taps
Clean water stored and piped to home taps, treatment cleans the water, raw water drawn to the treatment works, rain collected in a reservoir
Rain collected in a reservoir, clean water piped to home taps, raw water drawn to the treatment works, treatment cleans the water
Treatment cleans the water, rain collected in a reservoir, clean water stored, raw water drawn to the treatment works

questions.explanation: The whole animation runs the supply in that order: s1 reservoir, s2 drawn to the treatment works, s3 treatment stage by stage, s4 stored and piped to home taps.
